extracted.intended_audience: mathematics department faculty and undergraduate program assessment coordinators
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and standards for designing, administering, scoring, and using outcomes assessment for undergraduate mathematics and statistics majors (instruments, program goals, surveys, portfolios, comprehensive tests, and use of findings).

rubrics_metrics.name: Core curriculum cognitive expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Expectations relative to the core courses: the ability to link and integrate concepts, the ability to compare and contrast within a conceptual framework, the ability to analyze situations, the ability to conjecture and test hypotheses, formation of reasoning patterns, and the gaining of insights useful in problem solving.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The core courses (and thus the assessment) should maximize focus on student cognitive activity and growth attributable to concept exposure, independent of the course instructor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instrument item selection criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Selection of items was based on two criteria: there should be a mix of problem formats, and approximately half of the questions should be nonstandard (not typically used on in-class examinations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The investigators independently formulated a pool of items in formats including true/false, multiple choice, and free response, refined items, and selected parts intended to cover complementary topic areas (e.g., Part I: functions and calculus; Part II: linear algebra, statistics, discrete mathematics, algebraic structures).

rubrics_metrics.name: Nonstandard question types (design examples)
rubrics_metrics.description: Nonstandard questions asked students to find errors in sample work (e.g., locate an incorrect integral substitution), extend beyond typical cases (e.g., maximize area using flexible fencing), or tie together related ideas (e.g., give the function analogue of matrix inverse).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These questions often asked for justified examples or paragraph discussions. Students tended to attempt nonstandard items more often than standard items when unsure of standard procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment instrument length and balance
rubrics_metrics.description: Original instrument: Part I containing 21 items and Part II containing 18 items; each part designed to take 90 minutes. Revised finding: same basic information could be obtained using instruments with fewer items (12 to 15 questions, balanced between standard and nonstandard items) and a 60 minute examination period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shorter, balanced instruments (standard vs nonstandard) are recommended to reduce administration time while retaining diagnostic value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administration protocol for student testing
rubrics_metrics.description: Subjects were students who had completed appropriate core components, encouraged to participate on a voluntary basis during an evening session; students were not instructed to study or prepare, and were encouraged to give as much written information as possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Faculty other than investigators selected subjects and administered instruments. Samples were small (10–15) but represented cross-sections of departmental majors. Responses were authentic and generally serious. Note: inter-rater reliability and statistical item analysis were not formally addressed in this pilot.

rubrics_metrics.name: Score 3
rubrics_metrics.description: Conceptual understanding apparent; consistent notation, with only an occasional error; logical formulation; complete or near-complete solution/response.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used by investigators to identify responses demonstrating strong conceptual understanding and near-complete solutions. Differences in interpretation were resolved jointly through discussion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Score 2
rubrics_metrics.description: Conceptual understanding only adequate; careless mathematical errors present (algebra, arithmetic, for example); some logical steps lacking; incomplete solution/response.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applied to responses showing adequate understanding but marred by procedural or minor errors and missing steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Score 1
rubrics_metrics.description: Conceptual understanding not adequate; procedural errors; logical or relational steps missing; poor response or no response to the question posed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assigned when conceptual understanding is insufficient and key logical steps are absent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Score 0
rubrics_metrics.description: Does not attempt problem or conceptual understanding totally lacking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used for blank or wholly irrelevant responses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maximize cognitive activity independent of instructor
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment and core courses should maximize focus on student cognitive activity and growth attributable to concept exposure, independent of the course instructor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessment instruments and curricula should be designed to measure students' conceptual abilities rather than instructor-specific teaching artifacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program-level intended outcomes (B.S. statistics)
rubrics_metrics.description: Students completing the undergraduate degree in statistics should have a broad understanding of the discipline, a clear comprehension of the theoretical basis of statistical reasoning, and proficiency in the use of modern statistical methods and computing; ability to apply and convey statistical concepts orally and in writing; technical background for entry-level statistics positions; and adequate preparation for advanced study for academically talented students.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These program aims should drive selection of assessment measures and curriculum design.

rubrics_metrics.name: Knowledge of mathematical and theoretical basis
rubrics_metrics.description: Graduates should have knowledge of calculus (through multivariable calculus), matrix theory, and probability and mathematical statistics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measured via course performance, standardized exams, and course-specific assessments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Knowledge of statistical methods commonly used in practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Graduates should know analysis of variance, design of experiments, design of statistical surveys, and multiple regression.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessed through coursework, projects, and employer/graduate surveys indicating preparedness to use these methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Competency in modern statistical computing
rubrics_metrics.description: Graduates should have facility with one or more statistical packages (e.g., SAS, SPSS) and be capable of using modern graphical and display methods with real data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes simulation, graphical visualization, and use of computing resources; measured by computing coursework, projects, and demonstration of skills.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ability to summarize and present statistical results to non-experts
rubrics_metrics.description: Graduates should be able to summarize and present the results of a statistical study, orally or in writing, to an educated but not necessarily statistically expert audience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessment via writing assignments, oral presentations, employer feedback, and inclusion of communication tasks in methods courses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proficiency in an application area or data type
rubrics_metrics.description: Graduates should have proficiency in the use of statistics in a particular area of application or proficiency in the statistical analysis of a particular type of data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encouraged via elective specialization, internships, and applied project-based modules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grade-distribution monitoring by course category
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain and summarize distributions of B.S. graduates' grades (without names) for categories: (a) Mathematical and theoretical courses, (b) Statistical methods courses, (c) Computer science and statistical computing courses, (d) Statistics courses, (e) All courses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Annual summaries inform which areas students struggle with (e.g., theory vs methods) and feed into program improvements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Actuarial and standardized exam records
rubrics_metrics.description: Keep records of performance on standardized examinations (e.g., Actuarial Examinations 100 and 110) for students who take them as one measure of theoretical and applied competence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although few students may take these exams, results provide external benchmarks of student knowledge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record of summer internships
rubrics_metrics.description: Document summer undergraduate internships involving statistics in annual reports (employers, positions, rehiring outcomes).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Internship placement and subsequent hiring indicate program success in preparing students for real-world work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record of first positions or activities
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain records of first positions of graduates (grouped as commercial, governmental, manufacturing, graduate school, other) to monitor employability and alignment with program goals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Placements reflect readiness for entry-level positions and inform curriculum relevance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record of graduate degrees obtained
rubrics_metrics.description: Keep records of graduate degrees obtained by B.S. graduates and institutions to monitor preparation for advanced study.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Serves as evidence of program success in preparing students for graduate education.

rubrics_metrics.name: Survey of employers of graduates
rubrics_metrics.description: Survey employers/supervisors to obtain evaluations of graduates' educational background, strengths, weaknesses, and recommendations for program improvement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employers rated overall quality and highlighted needs (e.g., real-world applications, communication skills, substantive domain knowledge). Use responses to target curricular changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Survey of graduates (alumni)
rubrics_metrics.description: Administer surveys to recent graduates to determine employment, graduate education, and evaluations of how well program courses prepared them for work or study.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use returned surveys to identify deficits (e.g., computing topics, communication) and guide course redesigns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communication and writing requirements and assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: Require a Junior/Senior level writing course in addition to freshman English and a speech course; incorporate writing projects in the statistical methods sequence; require that a sample of each graduate's technical writing be evaluated and placed in departmental file prior to graduation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assigned to address employer and graduate feedback calling for improved oral and written communication skills; writing projects include short summaries, newspaper-like articles explaining analyses, and group technical reports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Computing and instructional module improvements
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide computing resources (workstations) and develop instructional modules that implement modern statistical methods and visualization to expose students to computationally intensive methods and real-world problems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use grants and lab upgrades to teach simulation, graphical displays, and interactive exploration; redesign courses (e.g., survey sampling) to include hands-on simulation and analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative success factors for assessment programs
rubrics_metrics.description: Implementing outcomes assessment requires high-level administrative support, faculty senate support, financial and secretarial aid, and a faculty member assigned (about one course per year) to maintain records and carry out analyses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such duties should be assigned over multi-year terms (about four years) and backed by institutional resources to make assessment sustainable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Xavier assessment plan components
rubrics_metrics.description: Methods chosen for assessing the mathematics major: Portfolio, Course Grades, Course Evaluations, MFT (Major Field Test), Senior Presentation, Exit Questionnaire and Exit Interview, Alumni Survey and Alumni Questionnaire.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These elements together record students' growth from entry to graduation and provide multiple feedback mechanisms (students, faculty, university).

rubrics_metrics.name: Portfolio content and process (Xavier)
rubrics_metrics.description: Portfolios maintained by faculty advisors: each semester students submit final examinations and samples of their best work from each mathematics class; include copy of any research or expository paper in an upper level class. Additional standard documents include an entry profile, entry questionnaire, counseling forms, and advisor notes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entry profile contains math background, GPA, SAT/ACT/AP credits, placement scores; entrance questionnaire elicits student perceptions and expectations. Faculty collect portfolio samples during advising periods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Major Field Test (MFT) passing standard and retake policy (Xavier)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department has set as successful performance a score at the 60% mark or higher on the MFT. If the goal is not met, the Department undertakes an extensive study of the case and may recommend retake; after two unsuccessful MFT performances a student may request a departmental comprehensive examination; repeated failure may prompt advising toward a liberal arts degree.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department provides review sessions for seniors preparing for the MFT; the MFT provides individual and mean scores plus subscores to identify strengths/weaknesses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Senior presentation requirement (Xavier)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each senior must make an oral presentation: topic selected by the student with advisor approval; student must submit a written draft for a thirty-minute lecture; advisor provides feedback and sets up a practice session.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Senior presentations are intended to develop oral communication and synthesis skills and become an integral part of departmental assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Student notification of assessment expectations (Xavier)
rubrics_metrics.description: Freshman mathematics majors receive letters in the first weeks informing them they must maintain a portfolio, make an oral presentation during their senior year, and meet departmental standards for satisfactory performance on the MFT.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Early notification is used to set student expectations and encourage sustained engagement with program outcomes.
